column3: The Hebrew calls the envoys Hiram’s “servants,” says that they anointed Solomon using an active verb, and describes Hiram as loving David; BSB uses “envoys,” a passive anointing, and “a friend.”
The Hebrew ends “under the soles of my feet”; BSB says “under his feet.” The Hebrew uses a pronoun where BSB specifies “his enemies.”
The Hebrew says that Solomon will give the servants’ wages “to you”; BSB says that he will pay the servants.
The Hebrew says Hiram heard Solomon’s words; BSB says that he received Solomon’s message.
The Hebrew says “I have heard what you sent to me”; BSB uses “I have received your message.”
The Hebrew explicitly says “bread” for the household provision; BSB uses “food” and adds the exchange connection.
The Hebrew says “twenty cors” of beaten oil; BSB says “20,000 baths” of pure olive oil.
The Hebrew names the labor levy twice in two clauses; BSB combines them as conscripting a labor force of 30,000 men.
The Hebrew explicitly names Solomon and the work being done; BSB shortens these to “his” and “the workers.”
The Hebrew coordinates the king’s command and their moving the stones as actions; BSB makes quarrying the content of the command. It says “house,” where BSB uses “temple.”
